### Paper 5 : EDA, PPG and Skin Temperature as Predictive Signals for Mental Failure
 
During my research, I discovered that using EDA, PPG and skin temperature data, it is possible to predict the effects of mental fatigue (PMC, 2025). This is significant to our research question about continuously sensed physiological signals and how they can be meaningfully categorized. Cognitive tests and 43 features were extracted from EDA, PPG and skin temperature signals in the study. The Kruskal–Wallis test and Mann–Whitney U test were then applied to these features to analyze them. Nearly half of the features were found to have strong statistical evidence for distinguishing relaxed states from altered emotional states. Further, 15 features were found to possess enough information to identify both mental workload and stress at the same time. This gives me a solid statistical basis for my research since it can help determine the physiological characteristics that most effectively distinguish the stress from the non-stress condition, and directly support the threshold-based rules that we are developing.


### Paper 6 : Beyond EDA: A Systematic Review of Multimodal Sympathetic Nervous System Arousal Classification
 
HRV is basically an indicator of the activity of the parasympathetic nervous system, while EDA is an indicator of sympathetic nervous system activity (via sweat gland function). A combination of both systems can be measured using sensors and will provide a wider picture of an individual's situation and a more complete reconstruction of an autonomic state than either of the sensor signals. This paper supports the motivation for using EDA + RESP + TEMP, as opposed to heart rate.
